author: LBM1948
attribution: Photo: LBM1948, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ruy_Gonz%C3%A1lez_de_Clavijo.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: White enamel street plate with maroon serif lettering on a brick wall, Samarkand; KOʻCHASI curves along the arched lower tab. The oʻ mark here is a 9-shaped closing quote, stored as U+2019 ’ to match the glyph (standard spelling uses ʻ U+02BB). Uzbek Latin spelling of Ruy González de Clavijo.

attribution: Photo: Екатерина Борисова, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%D0%9A%D0%BE%D0%BA%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B4._%D0%9C%D0%B5%D1%87%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%8C_%D0%AF%D0%BD%D0%B3%D0%B8_%D0%A7%D0%BE%D1%80%D1%81%D1%83_03.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Weathered blue street plate on a wall in Kokand (near Yangi Chorsu mosque); paint drips and rust run over the letters but the text is complete. The oʻ in KOʻCHASI is a turned-comma mark, stored as U+02BB ʻ.

author: PJakopin
attribution: Photo: PJakopin, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:House_number_sign_in_Dehibolo_2021.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Uzbek house-number plate over a door in Dehibolo village: MFY (mahalla fuqarolar yigʻini, neighbourhood) name, street name + KOʻCHASI (street), and on the blue right panel the flag, Oʻzbekiston and house number 34 + UY (house). Both oʻ letters are printed with a grave-accent-like stroke (`), stored as U+0060 to match the glyph; the standard spelling uses ʻ (U+02BB).

author: Екатерина Борисова
attribution: Photo: Екатерина Борисова, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%D0%9A%D0%BE%D0%BA%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B4._%D0%9E%D0%B1%D0%BE%D0%B4_%D1%8E%D1%80%D1%82_109_04.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Uzbek house-number plate on a plastered wall in Kokand: street name + KOʻCHASI on the white panel, flag, OʻZBEKISTON and house number 109 on the blue panel. Both oʻ use a turned-comma (6-shaped) mark, stored as U+02BB ʻ. Plate is small in the frame.

author: Ji-Elle
attribution: Photo: Ji-Elle, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tashkent-Museum_of_Applied_Arts_(2).jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.

lines.text: MINISTRY OF CULTURAL AFFAIRS AND SPORTS

notes: Black plaque with raised metal letters and the state emblem, Museum of Applied Arts, Tashkent; slightly from below. MUZEYI is letter-spaced (M U Z E Y I). The mark in SANʻAT is a raised 6-shaped (turned-comma) tick, stored as U+02BB ʻ as it appears, although standard spelling is sanʼat with U+02BC ʼ; the tick in OʻZBEKISTON is tiny and its exact shape is not certain. The U of MUSEUM and the E of APPLIED are slightly displaced/damaged.

author: Akhemen
attribution: Photo: Akhemen, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bilingual_Samarkand.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Painted entrance arch of Boʻzi mahalla (neighbourhood), Samarkand. Top beam: the name in double quotes printed as two closing-style marks ” ... ” (U+201D), and the oʻ mark is a grave-like stroke stored as U+0060 to match the glyph. The two side posts carry 'XUSH KELIBSIZ' (Uzbek, left) and 'ХУШ ОМАДЕД' (Tajik Cyrillic, right) written vertically, one letter per row; word spaces are inferred because the stacking leaves no clear gap. Two cars under the arch show plates incidentally.

author: Humoyun Mehridinov
attribution: Photo: Humoyun Mehridinov, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:A_sign_in_the_Tashkent_Botanical_Garden.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Engraved wooden fingerposts in the Tashkent Botanical Garden. Target lines are the lower-left board (Europe/Crimea/Caucasus exposition, left arrow) and the right board (Amfiteatr, straight ahead). The upper-left board 'Shimo..y Amerika ekspozitsiyasi / Экспозиция Северной Америки' is a partial-read distractor: a wood knot hides the letters between 'Shimo' and 'y' (presumably Shimoliy), so it is not transcribed. A worn patch also blurs the 'sp' of 'ekspozitsiyasi' on the lower board. Small 'Навигация от mytaxi' sponsor tag below is a distractor. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.
source_title: File:A sign in the Tashkent Botanical Garden.jpg

author: Solijon Solayev
attribution: Photo: Solijon Solayev, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Yangiariq_tumani.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Blue letters on a white entry-gate structure marking the border of Yangiariq district (Xorazm region). The sign may continue beyond the right edge of the frame (e.g. a 'TUMANI' word); only YANGIARIQ is visible, its Q touching the edge. The image looks digitally upscaled/smoothed. Two heads at the bottom edge are incidental. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Humoyun Mehridinov
attribution: Photo: Humoyun Mehridinov, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Beautiful_Sign_in_Tashkent_Botanical_Garden.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Two engraved wooden fingerposts (left arrows) in the Tashkent Botanical Garden. The gʻ in 'Togʻ' is written with a turned-comma mark (6-shaped), stored here as U+02BB ʻ. Russian 'Зеленый' is written with е, not ё. Same garden and sign family as c132651919 but different boards and destinations. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.
source_title: File:Beautiful Sign in Tashkent Botanical Garden.jpg

author: Bgag
attribution: Photo: Bgag, CC0 1.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Welcome_board_in_Kokand.jpg. License: http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/deed.en. Unmodified original.
notes: City welcome board in Kokand: a framed banner with Uzbek and English text above large red 3D letters 'WELCOME TO KOKAND'. The oʻ in Qoʻqonga is a turned-comma (6-shaped) mark, stored as U+02BB ʻ. Double space in 'of  the world!' as printed. The banner photo of Khudayar Khan's palace is decoration. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Nataev
attribution: Photo: Nataev, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Nurota_District_sign.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Hillside district-border sign on the Qoraqargʻa pass, Nurota District, seen from the road at a distance (small in frame). Large 3D letters NUROTA with a mountain logo whose peak forms the N; blue strip below reads 'XUSH KELIBSIZ' (left), 'TUMANI' (centre, completing 'Nurota tumani' = Nurota district), 'WELCOME!' (right). location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.
